prompt: We're starting a brand new project. Walk me through the whole software development lifecycle and which of your skills apply at each stage.
Review this pull request before we merge it. Is it clean?
Help me write documentation that actually survives: README, API docs, changelog.
We keep arguing about whether to over-engineer this module. Which engineering principles apply here?
Record the decision we just made about migrating to a modular monolith. Where do we write it down?
This new endpoint takes untrusted input from the internet. What's the baseline security checklist I must apply?
This OrderService class parses, validates, persists, and emails. How should I split it and fix the dependency direction?
Design the API for a new orders resource: which style, what status codes and error shape, and how do we make retries safe?
Our checkout touches three services. We need the sagas, the outbox, and to stop retry storms from cascading outages.
Design the schema for these tables, tell me where to index, and plan the migration to add a column without breaking production.
We're adding a topic for order_placed events. Consumers duplicate work and we can't replay history. Set this flow up correctly.
The request is slow and there's no measurement. Someone proposed a cache, but I want to profile first. Run the performance loop.
This bug needs fixing: write the regression test, watch it fail, then implement — red, green, refactor.
The code works but is a 500-line god class that's painful to change. Restructure it without changing any behavior.
This ask is vague: 'make login better'. Turn it into user stories, acceptance criteria, edge cases, and explicit non-goals.
Design the high-level shape of the new system before code: components, ownership boundaries, data flow, and the trade-offs between the options.
Engineers and business use different words for the same concepts and we can't agree on our models. How do we align boundaries and language?
Structure the app backbone so business logic is not tangled with the framework and the database — testable core, dependency rule, ports and adapters.
Our objects need configurable variants per environment. Which pattern fits this problem shape, and what does it cost us?
The team wants to split the monolith into microservices. Work out whether the split earns its cost and where the ownership boundaries should be.
Our public API spec drifted from the implementation and clients break silently. Set up contract-first design with versioning and compatibility policy.
The requirement just says 'fast and reliable'. Give me quantified non-functional targets we can design and verify against.
CI takes 40 minutes and misses failures that staging catches. Restructure the pipeline stages, gates, and artifact flow.
Our Docker image is 1.5GB, contains a compiler, and runs as root. Fix the Dockerfile properly.
Pods keep restarting in loops and rollouts have no rollback story. Review the deployment manifests, probes, and resources.
We provision infrastructure from laptops and the state file lives on someone's machine. Set up safe infrastructure as code.
Deployments are imperative scripts and the cluster always drifts from the repo. Move us to declarative Git-driven delivery.
Production debugging means grepping unstructured logs across services. Make our running system observable: logs, metrics, traces.
The pager is noisy and there's no SLO anywhere. Design alerting around error budgets with actionable runbooks.
The pipeline ships code with no static analysis, and a leaked secret is sitting in git history. Harden the delivery supply chain.
We deploy straight to 100% with feature work half-exposed and rollback means panic. Set up proper release management.
We need a testing plan for this release: where the test budget goes, coverage goals, and what to automate vs keep manual.
This discount rule has ranges, boundaries, and condition combinations. Derive the systematic test case set from it.
Our unit tests mock every collaborator and break on any rename. Write fast, honest, behavior-asserting unit tests.
Unit tests are green but the repository breaks against the real database. Wire the integration tests at the real seams.
Pick the few user journeys that prove checkout works through the real stack and make them stable against flake.
Verify this API's surface against its spec: schemas, auth flows, edge cases, and the failing shapes.
We need evidence our latency targets hold: build the load model, then load, stress, and soak tests against it.
A regression escaped to production and the suite is full of flaky tests. Design the regression selection and fix the flakes.

The frontend is one big components folder plus a hooks folder and every feature is tangled in both. Restructure the frontend codebase into feature-based modules with clean layers and folder conventions for module boundaries.
This Card component has twenty props and growing conditionals. Redesign it using composition, with explicit prop and event contracts and a presentational versus container split.
We're choosing how to manage state for the new checkout: where does local state live, when does state become global, and how is server state cached separately from a store?
Set up the API integration for the settings screen: fetching and caching server data, loading and error handling with retries, and optimistic updates for the toggle.
The dialog only works with a mouse and fails WCAG. Fix the semantics, keyboard navigation, ARIA, focus management, and contrast for AA.
This layout breaks on small screens and the breakpoint list is out of control. Make it responsive with a mobile-first base, a fluid layout, and container queries for the sidebar components.
The homepage feels slow: LCP regressed and the bundle keeps growing. Analyze it against the Core Web Vitals: bundle analysis, rendering cost, memoization, and image optimization.
The app renders user content and embeds a third-party widget. Audit the frontend security: XSS, CSRF, sanitization, secure headers, and client-side secret hygiene.
